title: Adaptive Request-ID Gateway and Telemetry Bridge
creator: Ava Lin
description: Implement a lightweight, adaptive Request-ID gateway + Telemetry Bridge to improve cross-service request attribution while keeping SDK overhead under 1% CPU for hot paths. Goals: 1) provide a deterministic request identifier that survives protocol transitions (HTTP/gRPC/websocket/worker queues), 2) support sampling hints and minimal baggage for downstream tracing, 3) act as a backpressure-aware gate that avoids unbounded per-request state for long-running streaming responses. Deliverables: SDK middleware (Node/Python/Go), server-side middleware for Edge and runtime, migration guide, unit + load tests, dashboard updates for latency/error attribution.
acceptance_criteria: New Request-ID header generated when missing and preserved when present across service hops
SDK middleware exposes getRequestContext() with request_id and sampling_hint without blocking fast paths
End-to-end integration test demonstrating header preservation across HTTP->gRPC->worker-queue
No more than 1% p99 CPU increase on microbenchmark for Node SDK path
Console dashboard shows request_id as a dimension for latency and error drilldown
design_notes: Use compact 128-bit hyphenless base62 request_id format to reduce header size and logging verbosity
Prefer header name: x-rw-request-id and set traceparent compatibility mapping for Otel-friendly environments
Telemetry Bridge will translate existing baggage keys to a small stable set (rid, sh) where sh = sampling hint
For streaming paths, implement 'dehydration' policy: when active token count grows past threshold, encode minimal state and drop heavy baggage to avoid memory amplification
Backpressure gate will annotate request with lifecycle events (queued, active, drained) but avoid allocating per-request goroutines in runtime path
implementation_plan: Spike: implement header generator and context carrier in Node SDK (2d)
SDK middleware: Node/Python/Go adapters exposing requestContext API (3d)
Runtime: edge middleware to normalize headers and populate internal carrier (2d)
Load test and perf tuning, measure CPU and latency impact (2d)
Docs + migration guide + console dashboard update (2d)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: header name collision with customer headers — mitigation: use x-rw- prefix and document in SDK headers whitelist
Risk: added per-request allocations on hot path — mitigation: use object pools and inline fast-path that returns a small struct by value
Risk: sampling mismatches across services — mitigation: sampling_hint is advisory; runtime will reconcile and emit sampling-change events to tracing pipeline
Risk: long-running streams accumulate baggage — mitigation: dehydration policy triggers after NKB of payload or time threshold and emits an event to logs/traces
metrics_and_dashboards: Add tag/dimension: request_id on latency and error dashboards (enable sampling for cardinality control)
Dashboard: 'Request Flow' showing cross-protocol hops with counts and median latency by service
Alert: spike in dehydration events > 5% of requests for 10m => pager on-call platform team
tests: Integration: cross-protocol propagation harness using local test services
Perf: 1M requests benchmark comparing current SDK vs new middleware path
Chaos: simulate worker queue requeue and ensure request_id remains stable
notes: Related infra ticket: ENG-472891 (context-reconciler) provides a shared carrier format
Confirmed with Security: pre-review requested due to header canonicalization and KMS usage for signing (see security ticket)
